correctness.rationale: Every generation-n atom is an interval of diameter at most L lambda^n. An explicit induction from disjoint closed branch images and common absolute affine slope gives pairwise distance at least g lambda^(n-1), with no finite-experiment extrapolation. Dense basic-component orbits imply a bijection of active atoms with itinerary factors. Applying the published eventual affine word-complexity theorem at floor/ceiling scales establishes a uniform O(1) remainder and the exact coefficient. Periodic components are finite and handled separately; endpoint strictness is ensured.

value.rationale: Both finite orbits and minimal Cantor components have Hausdorff/box dimension zero in the originating setting, so ordinary dimensions do not quantify how aperiodicity survives geometrically. The exact finite positive logarithmic cover coefficient detects nonperiodic minimal components and equals a discrete left/right discontinuity recurrence count scaled by the metric contraction exponent. It is a natural invariant across the class and not an arbitrary finite parameter test.
